page0.text:
"...Man."
I sigh and lean against a sign.
I searched around until the sun set, and the only thing I found out was how useless I am.

page1.text:
"Ugh..."
The wound on my left shoulder is aching.
I don't know if it's because my bandage is getting loose or if the wound itself opened up.
...Anyway, I can't waste any more time.
If I can't find a certain lead, then it'll end up just like last night.

page2.text:
"...Geez, where could she be?"
...I recall when I parted ways with her last night.
It's been a day already since she told me exactly what was on her mind, like how I can't fight without Saber or how I should escape to the church.

page3.text:
"...Oh yeah, the church."
There is a lead.
I thought about it when I went out to town this morning.
The supervisor of the Holy Grail War.
The priest at the church on the hill should know about Tohsaka's whereabouts...

page4.text: "...It's irritating to go ask for his help, but now's not the time to be picky..."

page5.text:
...No, whether I like him or not, I shouldn't go see that priest.
He says he's a priest, but there's something unsettling about him that tells me Kirei Kotomine is a man that fundamentally shouldn't be approached.
I don't want to have to ask for his advice if possible, but he's the only one I can rely on.

page6.text:
"...It's just once. That shouldn't be a problem."
I tell myself and move my aching body.
It's 7 PM.

page7.text:
I walk to the train station for twenty minutes.
The church stands in the suburbs, away from the noisy town.
...
It's been nine days since I last went up this hill.
However, considering the fact that I had never come here prior to that, I'm coming here quite often now.

page8.text:
...To be honest, I don't like that church.
Maybe more than Kirei Kotomine, that church itself is forbidden territory that should not be approached.
The fire ten years ago.
It's because the church, which looked after the children that became orphans, forces me to recall that incident from ten years ago.

page9.text:
I finish going up the hill and go out into the open grounds.
"...!"
I suddenly get a headache.
It's not because of my left shoulder's wound.
The wound is causing me to have a fever, but it shouldn't give me this stabbing headache.

page10.text:
"Khh..."
My temple hurts.
I lose myself and feel a chill, as if my body is going to split in half like a shedding insect.

page11.text:
"...This is weird."
I fight through my headache and start running.
The cause is the hunch I have had since yesterday.
The unknown feeling that Tohsaka is in Shinto.
That has expanded to the max and is causing this headache.
Then... There is no doubt that something is going on in there...

page12.text:
There are bloodstains on the floor.
The traces of blood sporadically continue up to the door at the back of the church.
"...No, that's not it. It's not continuing into the back, but it seems like it's coming out from the back."

page13.text:
...It bothers me, but now is not the time for that.
The bloodstains mean that someone is hurt.
And this much too... Their life must be in danger.
...
I feel a sharp pain in my head. A dull heaviness settles into my body.
I ignore them as I take out my bamboo sword and start walking quietly.

page14.text:
"Tohsaka... Are you there?"
Nobody replies.
The air is tense.
I feel like all the windows in the church would shatter if I raised my voice.

page15.text:
...
I follow the traces of blood.
The bloodstains are in the crevices of the building.
It continues to the dark staircase that you would miss if you didn't know about it.

page16.text:
"...Stairs that lead underground... I didn't know this place had a basement."
This is a church, so could it be a mausoleum?
"Guh..."
...I can't afford to be leisurely pondering right now.
I exercise utmost caution and step into the darkness.

page17.text:
I descend in the darkness.
...There is a dim light at the end of the stairs.
I hold my breath and move forward, using only the light below as a guide.

page18.text:
The narrow corridor ends, and I come out to an open space.
It is a spacious stone chamber.
The stairs along the wall stretch down to the sanctuary.
There, stairs lead to an open space that seems like the sanctuary,
and there... is the one I had been looking for, Rin Tohsaka.

page19.text:
Tohsaka is confronting the enemy in front of her, with Archer protecting her.
In front of her... In front of the altar are two silhouettes.

page20.text:
It doesn't even have to be said.
The mage in the purple robe, Caster, and her Master, Kuzuki.
On the altar behind them...
There is Saber, who is looking down and panting painfully.

page21.text:
...
My heart skips a beat.
My pulse is clearly beating at a much faster rate.

page22.text:
...
The situation is obvious.
The two pairs of Master and Servant confronting each other in the sanctuary about five meters below me.
They haven't noticed me hiding overhead, as they're too preoccupied.

page23.text:
Tohsaka and Caster are both thinking ahead, looking for an opening to attack.
To look up in a situation like this would not be allowed.

page24.text:
...
My heart beats even faster.
My headache is constant, and I feel an intense pain in my shoulder as if it's been seared by a hot iron.

page25.text:
I can't keep my presence hidden forever in this state.
Caster or Kuzuki. If one of them looks up even just a bit, they'll notice me hiding.
I...
